title: RAID Log (Risks, Assumptions, Issues, Dependencies)
description: The four-letter document that separates the projects that recover from the projects that don't. Keep it dry, keep it dated, keep it true.

worked_examples.title: Partner-portal — pre-launch week
worked_examples.content_md:
## RAID log — partner-portal — week 11

### Risks

| ID | Risk | Impact | Likelihood | Owner | Mitigation | Status | Last updated |
|----|------|--------|------------|-------|------------|--------|--------------|
| R1 | Document OCR accuracy on non-UK receipts may drop below 85% | M | M | Sam | Restrict to UK at launch; add foreign in Phase 2 | Open | Mon |
| R2 | Partner onboarding volume on launch day exceeds support team capacity | H | L | Diego | Soft launch to 20% of partners first | Open | Mon |
| R3 | FCA AML guidance changes between scoping and launch (already added 4 fields once) | M | L | Marcus | Quarterly compliance review baked into roadmap | Open | Mon |

### Assumptions

| ID | Assumption | Validated? | Source | Owner | Status | Last updated |
|----|-----------|------------|--------|-------|--------|--------------|
| A1 | OCR vendor's 94% accuracy claim holds in production | No | Vendor proposal | Sam | Test post-launch + monthly audit | Open | Mon |
| A2 | Partner success team can handle a 4hr manual-review SLA at launch volume | Yes | Capacity model run by ops | Ops | Closed — model validated | Closed | Wed |
| A3 | The existing identity service can carry the additional load without scaling work | No | Engineering estimate, not load-tested | Sam | Load test booked for Thursday | Open | Mon |

### Issues

| ID | Issue | Impact | Owner | Resolution | Status | Last updated |
|----|-------|--------|-------|-----------|--------|--------------|
| I1 | Consent string missing legitimate-interest disclosure (3 places) | M | Me | Copy fix in flight, EOD Tuesday | In progress | Tue |
| I2 | Stand-up has slipped 15 minutes for three days running | L | Diego | Re-set start time + standing 25-min cap | In progress | Wed |

### Dependencies

| ID | Dependency | From | Needed by | Owner | Status | Last updated |
|----|-----------|------|-----------|-------|--------|--------------|
| D1 | Updated AML field schema sign-off | Compliance | Mon | Marcus | Confirmed Friday | Closed | Fri |
| D2 | Marketing launch email copy approved | Marketing | Wed | Marketing lead | Reviewed; in legal | In progress | Tue |
| D3 | Support team trained on the new portal flows | Ops | Wed | Ops | One session Mon, one Wed | In progress | Mon |

annotations.note: Note the Last Updated column on every row. A RAID item without a recent date isn't being managed — it's being collected. Audit your log monthly for stale items.
Risks are framed as one sentence each. If you can't compress the risk to a sentence, you don't understand it yet. Write it long, then cut.
R3 is the regulatory-trend risk — the one that's low-likelihood per quarter but high-impact when it lands. Worth keeping on the log even when it feels distant.
Assumptions are the most-forgotten of the four. A2 here is the kind that should be validated before launch, not after. Closing it deliberately is part of the work.

common_mistakes: Writing risks at a level that can't be acted on. "Things may go wrong with the launch" is not a risk. "OCR accuracy may drop below 85% on non-UK receipts" is.

Mixing risks and issues. A risk is something that hasn't happened yet. An issue is something that has. When a risk lands, move it to the Issues table — don't leave it in Risks marked "closed: happened".
Letting assumptions live forever. Every assumption should have a date by which it gets validated. "Yes — closed Wed" is the goal, not "Open — for three months".
RAID logs that nobody reads. Send the diff weekly, not the whole document. Highlight what's new + what's moved + what's closed.
variant_patterns: Compliance variant: add a Regulatory Reference column to the Risks table so each risk is tied to the specific regulation or standard it threatens.
Cross-org variant: split Dependencies into Internal (from teams you can ping) and External (from vendors / partners with their own timelines) — they need different cadences.
